note: Production seed for the three missing structured games plus ten lower-level-first games.

activities.title: Number Mission
activities.summary: Numbers become information you must confirm, correct and use with another person.
activities.instructions: Use the visible facts to complete a real mini-mission. Listen carefully and repair any number that does not match.
activities.student_intro: Numbers matter here. Check them, repeat them and correct mistakes.

prompts.text: Confirm the café order using the numbers.
prompts.title: Café order check
prompts.instructions: Check the order with your teacher until every number matches.
prompts.situation: You ordered quickly and the server may have written one detail incorrectly.
prompts.outcome: Confirm the full order and correct one mismatch.

challenge.text: The total you hear is wrong. Correct it politely.

role_swap.instruction: Swap roles and use the same facts in a new order.

teacher.private_cue: Read one quantity back incorrectly after the learner checks it.
teacher.final_confirmation: The final order is 2 coffees, 1 sandwich, €9.50.

prompts.teacher_note: Keep this conversational. A0 learners can use chunks rather than full questions.

prompts.text: Confirm the train details before you leave.
prompts.title: Train check
prompts.instructions: Ask and confirm until you have the correct platform, time, carriage and seat.
prompts.situation: You are at the station and want to make sure you copied everything correctly.

challenge.text: The platform changes at the last minute. Confirm the new platform.

role_swap.instruction: Swap roles and confirm the details again.

teacher.private_cue: First say platform 8, then let the learner correct you.

prompts.teacher_note: Focus on intelligible number pronunciation and repair.

prompts.text: Check the appointment details.
prompts.title: Appointment check
prompts.instructions: Confirm the day, date, time and room.
prompts.situation: The receptionist is checking an appointment you booked online.
prompts.outcome: Leave with one clear set of appointment details.

challenge.text: The time moves 30 minutes later. Repeat the updated appointment.

role_swap.instruction: Swap roles and confirm a new appointment.

prompts.teacher_note: A1 learners may point/read then reformulate.

prompts.text: Confirm a delivery before it arrives.
prompts.title: Delivery details
prompts.instructions: Check quantities, address number and arrival time.
prompts.situation: A small delivery is coming to your workplace.
prompts.outcome: Confirm exactly what is coming and when.

challenge.text: Two extra boxes are added. Update the quantity and confirm it again.

role_swap.instruction: Swap roles and repeat with one changed number.

prompts.teacher_note: Keep the interaction fast and practical.

activities.title: Picture Detective
activities.summary: Ask simple questions about pictures until you can identify the secret one.
activities.instructions: Study the pictures. Ask useful questions and identify the teacher’s secret picture.
activities.student_intro: Look first. Ask questions. Guess only when you have enough information.

prompts.text: Find the secret everyday object.
prompts.title: Everyday objects
prompts.instructions: Ask questions until you can identify the secret picture.

challenge.text: Choose your own secret object and let the teacher guess.

role_swap.instruction: Choose a new secret picture and swap roles.

prompts.teacher_note: Answer with simple yes/no or short chunks. Do not name the secret.

prompts.text: Find the secret food or drink.
prompts.title: Snack detective
prompts.instructions: Ask about colour, type, temperature or when people eat it.

challenge.text: Describe one picture without saying its name.

role_swap.instruction: Choose a new picture and swap roles.

options.label: mug
options.image_alt: A mug with a hot drink

prompts.teacher_note: Allow A0 learners to use single-word adjective + question chunks.

prompts.text: Find the secret way to travel.
prompts.title: Transport detective
prompts.instructions: Ask questions about wheels, speed, people and where it goes.

challenge.text: Ask only three questions before you guess.

role_swap.instruction: Swap roles and choose a new transport picture.

prompts.text: Find the secret picture without labels.
prompts.title: No-label round
prompts.instructions: Use what you can see. Ask category and use questions before guessing.
support: Would I use it at home?
Can I put things inside it?

challenge.text: Now explain why each wrong option cannot be the secret.

role_swap.instruction: Choose a new secret picture and swap roles.

options.label: mug
options.image_alt: A mug with a hot drink

prompts.teacher_note: Do not reveal labels verbally unless the learner is stuck.

activities.title: Make the Choice
activities.summary: Compare simple options, choose one and explain what matters most.
activities.instructions: Compare the options, choose one and explain your reason. The teacher may reveal a new condition.
activities.student_intro: There is no perfect answer. Choose what works best for you.

prompts.text: Choose the best lunch for you.
prompts.title: Lunch break
prompts.instructions: Compare the two options and choose one.

challenge.text: You now have only 15 minutes. Does your choice change?

material.situation: You have a short lunch break.
material.task: Choose the option that works best for you.

teacher.role_note: Ask which matters more: time, price or hunger.

prompts.text: Choose how to go to class.
prompts.title: Bus or bike?

teacher.role_note: Ask the learner whether speed still matters most.

prompts.teacher_note: Encourage comparative forms but accept simple reasons.

prompts.text: Choose a weekend plan.
prompts.title: Saturday plan
prompts.instructions: Compare cost, energy and social time.

challenge.text: A friend can join only one option. Reconsider your choice.

material.task: Pick the plan you want most.

teacher.complication: Your friend can join only the cinema plan.
teacher.role_note: Ask whether company changes the decision.

prompts.teacher_note: Let learner choose personally or hypothetically.

prompts.text: Choose a gift.
prompts.title: Birthday gift
prompts.instructions: Choose a gift based on price and what the person likes.

challenge.text: You discover the person already owns one option.

role_swap.instruction: Teacher chooses; learner asks for a reason.

material.situation: Your friend likes music and reading.

teacher.complication: Your friend already owns the book.
teacher.role_note: Ask whether price still changes the decision.

activities.title: Quick Pick
activities.summary: Fast A/B/C choices that force a short spoken decision and one reason.
activities.instructions: Choose one option quickly. Say it aloud and add one short reason.
activities.student_intro: Pick fast. One answer, one reason.

prompts.text:
Breakfast tomorrow:
A) eggs
B) yogurt
C) toast
prompts.student_support: I choose ___ because it is ___.
prompts.challenge: Choose a second option for a very busy morning.

prompts.text:
Go to the city centre:
A) bus
B) bike
C) walk
prompts.student_support: I choose ___ because it is fast / cheap / easy.
prompts.challenge: It starts raining. Pick again.
prompts.teacher_note: Elicit one simple comparative if possible.

prompts.text:
Free evening:
A) film
B) restaurant
C) stay home
prompts.student_support: I’d choose ___ because ___.
prompts.challenge: You are very tired. Pick again.

prompts.text:
Drink with lunch:
A) water
B) coffee
C) juice
prompts.student_support: For me, ___.
prompts.challenge: Now choose for a hot summer day.

prompts.text:
Meeting time:
A) 09:00
B) 13:00
C) 18:00
prompts.student_support: ___ is better for me because ___.
prompts.challenge: You have another appointment at 12:30.

prompts.text:
Take only one on a short trip:
A) book
B) headphones
C) camera
prompts.student_support: I’d take ___ because ___.
prompts.challenge: Your bag is very small.

activities.title: Ask to Unlock
activities.summary: Learners unlock hidden information by asking a small number of useful questions.
activities.instructions: The teacher knows the secret. Ask useful questions until you can unlock it.
activities.student_intro: You do not have the answer yet. Ask for it.

prompts.text: SECRET: a room in a house. Ask up to 4 questions and guess it.
prompts.student_support: Is it big? Is there a…? Do you cook/sleep there?
prompts.challenge: Ask only yes/no questions.
prompts.teacher_note: Secret answer: kitchen. Answer simply and consistently.

prompts.text: SECRET: a way to travel. Ask up to 4 questions and guess it.
prompts.student_support: Does it have wheels? Is it fast? Is it public?
prompts.challenge: You get only 3 questions.

prompts.text: SECRET: something I buy every week. Ask questions and guess it.
prompts.student_support: Is it food? Is it expensive? Where do you buy it?
prompts.challenge: Ask one question with how much / how many.

prompts.text: SECRET: where I went yesterday. Ask questions and guess the place.
prompts.student_support: Was it indoors? Did you buy something? Who did you go with?
prompts.challenge: Ask one past-simple question.

prompts.text: SECRET: what time my train leaves. Ask the questions you need.
prompts.student_support: What time…? Which train…? From which platform…?
prompts.challenge: Confirm the answer by repeating it back.

prompts.text: SECRET: my weekend plan. Ask questions until you can describe it.
prompts.student_support: Where are you going? Who with? What are you going to do?
prompts.challenge: Summarise the plan in one sentence.
prompts.teacher_note: Secret: Saturday morning market, lunch with a friend, cinema at 20:00.

activities.title: Oops, Fix Me!
activities.summary: The teacher says the wrong detail and the learner corrects it clearly and naturally.
activities.instructions: Read your real information. Listen to the teacher’s wrong version and correct it.
activities.student_intro: I’ll get it wrong on purpose. Fix me.

prompts.text:
YOUR INFO: Tuesday at 18:00
TEACHER SAYS: Monday at 19:00
prompts.student_support: No, it’s Tuesday at six.
prompts.challenge: Correct both details in one sentence.
prompts.teacher_note: Say the wrong line naturally, then let learner repair.

prompts.text:
YOUR INFO: 2 coffees and 1 sandwich
TEACHER SAYS: 1 coffee and 2 sandwiches
prompts.student_support: No, two coffees and one sandwich.
prompts.challenge: Add please and make it polite.

prompts.text:
YOUR INFO: Train at 14:20, platform 6
TEACHER SAYS: Train at 14:40, platform 9
prompts.student_support: Actually, it’s at… from platform…
prompts.challenge: Ask the teacher to repeat the final details.

prompts.text:
YOUR INFO: Room 308 for 3 nights
TEACHER SAYS: Room 380 for 2 nights
prompts.student_support: I think there are two mistakes…
prompts.challenge: Correct the teacher politely, not abruptly.

prompts.text:
YOUR INFO: Meeting starts at 10:30 in Room B
TEACHER SAYS: It starts at 11:30 in Room D
prompts.student_support: Just to clarify, it starts…
prompts.challenge: Confirm what time everyone should arrive.

prompts.text:
YOUR INFO: Total €24.50
TEACHER SAYS: Total €42.50
prompts.student_support: Sorry, I think the total is…
prompts.challenge: Ask how the teacher got the wrong total.

activities.title: Build My Day
activities.summary: Put a simple schedule into spoken order using times and sequencing language.
activities.instructions: Read the schedule and tell the teacher what happens in order.
activities.student_intro: Build the day one step at a time.

prompts.text:
08:00 breakfast
09:30 English class
13:00 lunch
18:00 gym
prompts.student_support: At eight, breakfast. Then…
prompts.challenge: Say the whole day without reading the times twice.

prompts.text:
07:30 wake up
08:15 bus
09:00 work
12:30 lunch
prompts.student_support: First I… Then I…
prompts.challenge: Add one thing after lunch.

prompts.text:
10:00 supermarket
11:30 coffee with Anna
14:00 clean the flat
20:00 film
prompts.student_support: In the morning… In the afternoon… In the evening…
prompts.challenge: Change one time and explain why.

prompts.text:
09:15 train
11:00 arrive in Florence
13:00 lunch
16:30 museum
19:10 train home
prompts.student_support: First we take… We arrive at…
prompts.challenge: Your train home moves to 18:40. Update the plan.

prompts.text:
08:30 check email
09:00 team meeting
11:00 client call
13:00 lunch
15:30 finish report
prompts.student_support: My first task is… After the meeting…
prompts.challenge: The client call moves to 10:00. Rebuild the morning.

prompts.text:
17:30 finish work
18:00 supermarket
19:00 cook dinner
20:30 call a friend
23:00 bed
prompts.student_support: After work… Later… Finally…
prompts.challenge: You finish work one hour late. What changes?

activities.title: Three Clues
activities.summary: Use three simple clues to describe a target without giving a long explanation.
activities.instructions: Use the three clues to help you describe the target. The teacher guesses.
activities.student_intro: Three clues. One target. Make me guess.

prompts.text:
TARGET: bicycle
CLUES: two wheels · outside · you ride it
prompts.student_support: It has… You use it…
prompts.challenge: Add one new clue of your own.
prompts.teacher_note: Do not guess immediately; let learner produce at least two chunks.

prompts.text:
TARGET: fridge
CLUES: kitchen · cold · food
prompts.student_support: It is in… It keeps…
prompts.challenge: Describe it without saying kitchen.

prompts.text:
TARGET: umbrella
CLUES: rain · hand · outside
prompts.student_support: You use it when…
prompts.challenge: Add a colour and a size.
prompts.teacher_note: Accept simple noun phrases at A0.

prompts.text:
TARGET: airport
CLUES: planes · passport · travel
prompts.student_support: You go there when…
prompts.challenge: Say two things people do there.

prompts.text:
TARGET: supermarket
CLUES: food · basket · pay
prompts.student_support: It is a place where…
prompts.challenge: Give one example of something you buy there.

prompts.text:
TARGET: colleague
CLUES: work · same company · person
prompts.student_support: A colleague is someone who…
prompts.challenge: Explain the difference between colleague and friend.

activities.title: What Changed?
activities.summary: Compare a before and after situation and say exactly what is different.
activities.instructions: Look at BEFORE and AFTER. Say what changed.
activities.student_intro: Spot the change and say it clearly.

prompts.text:
BEFORE: The café opens at 08:00.
AFTER: The café opens at 07:30.
prompts.student_support: Before: eight. Now: seven thirty.
prompts.challenge: Say whether the café opens earlier or later.

prompts.text:
BEFORE: I take the bus to work.
AFTER: I ride my bike to work.
prompts.student_support: Before I… Now I…
prompts.challenge: Add one possible reason for the change.

prompts.text:
BEFORE: The room has one table.
AFTER: The room has three tables.
prompts.student_support: There was one… Now there are three…
prompts.challenge: Add one more change yourself.
prompts.teacher_note: Accept there is/are if past form is too hard.

prompts.text:
BEFORE: The ticket costs €12.
AFTER: The ticket costs €18.
prompts.student_support: The price went from… to…
prompts.challenge: Say how much more expensive it is.

prompts.text:
BEFORE: We meet on Friday at 15:00.
AFTER: We meet on Thursday at 16:30.
prompts.student_support: The day changed from… The time changed from…
prompts.challenge: Confirm the new meeting in one sentence.

prompts.text:
BEFORE: Sara works from home five days a week.
AFTER: Sara works from home two days a week.
prompts.student_support: She used to / Before she… Now she…
prompts.challenge: Suggest one possible reason.
prompts.teacher_note: Do not require used to; it is optional support.

activities.title: Mini Map Mission
activities.summary: Use a tiny route mission to practise asking for and giving simple directions.
activities.instructions: Use START, END and the landmarks. Ask for or give the route.
activities.student_intro: Get from A to B using English.

prompts.text:
START: station
END: café
LANDMARKS: bank · park
MISSION: Ask the teacher how to get there.
prompts.student_support: Where is the café? Left or right?
prompts.challenge: Repeat the route back to the teacher.
prompts.teacher_note: Route: straight past the bank, café on the left before the park.

prompts.text:
START: hotel
END: supermarket
LANDMARKS: pharmacy · bus stop
MISSION: Ask for directions.
prompts.student_support: Go straight / turn left / next to…
prompts.challenge: Ask one clarification question.
prompts.teacher_note: Route: right at pharmacy, supermarket opposite bus stop.

prompts.text:
START: school
END: library
LANDMARKS: café · church
MISSION: Give the teacher directions.
prompts.student_support: First… Then… It’s next to…
prompts.challenge: Teacher takes a wrong turn; correct them.
prompts.teacher_note: Route: straight, left at café, library next to church.

prompts.text:
START: museum
END: restaurant
LANDMARKS: river · bridge
MISSION: Give the route in 3 steps.
prompts.student_support: Cross… Go along… Turn…
prompts.challenge: Now give the route back to the museum.
prompts.teacher_note: Route can be invented consistently from landmarks.

prompts.text:
START: office
END: car park
LANDMARKS: reception · lift
MISSION: Help a visitor find it.
prompts.student_support: Go past… Take the… It’s on your…
prompts.challenge: The lift is not working. Change the route.

prompts.text:
START: train station
END: city hall
LANDMARKS: square · fountain · bank
MISSION: Ask for directions, then summarise them.
prompts.student_support: So I go… then… and it’s…?
prompts.challenge: Ask how long it takes on foot.

activities.title: Pass It Back
activities.summary: Train conversational reciprocity: answer, then ask a connected question back.
activities.instructions: Answer the teacher’s question, then pass the conversation back with one connected question.
activities.student_intro: Answer it. Then send the conversation back.

prompts.text:
TEACHER: What do you usually eat for breakfast?
YOUR JOB: Answer, then ask me a connected question.
prompts.student_support: I usually… And you?
prompts.challenge: Ask a different question, not just ‘And you?’

prompts.text:
TEACHER: How do you come to class?
YOUR JOB: Answer, then ask me about transport.
prompts.student_support: I come by… How do you…?
prompts.challenge: Ask how long it takes.
prompts.teacher_note: Accept by bus / on foot chunks.

prompts.text:
TEACHER: What do you like doing at the weekend?
YOUR JOB: Answer, then ask one connected question.
prompts.student_support: I like… What do you like…?
prompts.challenge: Ask a follow-up about when or who with.

prompts.text:
TEACHER: What time do you usually finish work or study?
YOUR JOB: Answer, then ask me about my day.
prompts.student_support: I usually finish at… What time do you…?
prompts.challenge: React to my answer before asking again.
prompts.teacher_note: Add a reaction: really? / that’s late.

prompts.text:
TEACHER: What was the best part of your week?
YOUR JOB: Answer, then ask me a past question.
prompts.student_support: The best part was… What did you…?
prompts.challenge: Ask a second follow-up based on my answer.

prompts.text:
TEACHER: What are you going to do after this lesson?
YOUR JOB: Answer, then ask me about my plan.
prompts.student_support: I’m going to… What are you going to…?
prompts.challenge: Find one thing your plans have in common.

activities.title: Tiny Story Builder
activities.summary: Combine three simple story cards into a short connected story.
activities.instructions: Use WHO, WHERE and ACTION to build a tiny story. Connect the ideas instead of listing them.
activities.student_intro: Three cards become one little story.

prompts.text:
WHO: a tired waiter
WHERE: a train station
ACTION: loses a phone
prompts.student_support: The waiter was… He was at… Then…
prompts.challenge: Give the story a happy ending.

prompts.text:
WHO: a student
WHERE: a café
ACTION: meets an old friend
prompts.student_support: A student is in… Then…
prompts.challenge: Add one thing they talk about.
prompts.teacher_note: A0 can use present simple story.

prompts.text:
WHO: a tourist
WHERE: a supermarket
ACTION: cannot find the exit
prompts.student_support: First… Then… Finally…
prompts.challenge: Add a person who helps.

prompts.text:
WHO: two colleagues
WHERE: an office kitchen
ACTION: find a birthday cake
prompts.student_support: They were… They saw… Then…
prompts.challenge: The cake has the wrong name on it.

prompts.text:
WHO: a family
WHERE: a bus stop
ACTION: the bus does not come
prompts.student_support: They wait… After… So they decide…
prompts.challenge: It starts raining.

prompts.text:
WHO: a chef
WHERE: a small hotel
ACTION: receives 20 pizzas by mistake
prompts.student_support: At first… The problem was… In the end…
prompts.challenge: The pizzas are already paid for.

activities.title: Which One Fits?
activities.summary: Choose the most natural phrase for a concrete low-level situation, then say it aloud.
activities.instructions: Read the situation, choose the phrase that fits best and say it naturally.
activities.student_intro: Pick the phrase you would really use.

prompts.text:
You want a coffee in a café.
A) Coffee.
B) Can I have a coffee, please?
C) I need coffee now.
prompts.student_support: Which one sounds polite and normal?
prompts.challenge: Order a tea instead without reading.
prompts.teacher_note: B is strongest. A may be acceptable contextually but is less complete.

prompts.text:
You do not understand your teacher.
A) Again.
B) Sorry, could you say that again?
C) You speak more.
prompts.student_support: Choose the phrase that asks politely for repetition.
prompts.challenge: Ask the teacher to speak more slowly too.

prompts.text:
You need directions from a stranger.
A) Excuse me, where is the station?
B) Station where?
C) Tell station.
prompts.student_support: Think: get attention + question.
prompts.challenge: Ask where the nearest bus stop is.

prompts.text:
Your friend says: ‘I’m really tired.’
A) That’s nice.
B) Oh no. Long day?
C) Why you tired?
prompts.student_support: React first, then ask.
prompts.challenge: Keep the conversation going for one more turn.
prompts.teacher_note: B is the most natural supportive response.

prompts.text:
A colleague sends you a file you asked for.
A) Thanks, got it.
B) Finally.
C) I receive.
prompts.student_support: Choose the natural short work response.
prompts.challenge: Make it slightly more formal.

prompts.text:
A waiter brings the wrong drink.
A) Sorry, I ordered water.
B) Wrong.
C) You make mistake.
prompts.student_support: Be clear and polite.
prompts.challenge: Ask for the correct drink too.
prompts.teacher_note: A, then extend with Could I have…?
